operations.title: AI for business
operations.subtitle: Applied AI systems for real processes: catalogs, documents, internal support and financial communication.
operations.transparencyNote: Real cases: three built as AI Engineer at Wembley Studios (2023–2025) and one built in the Turing Datathon (2026). I now offer them as a freelance service.

pain.label: The pain
pain.text: Your purchasing or sales team wastes time searching for products across PDF catalogs, scattered spreadsheets, or slow ERPs. Every supplier query means lost minutes, reference errors, and customers waiting.

solution.label: The solution
solution.text: A conversational assistant that understands natural language ("I need a part compatible with model X") and searches simultaneously across all your catalogs, data sheets, and product databases. Integrated where your team already works: Teams, internal web, or ERP.

result.label: The result with a real client
result.text: Assistant deployed for a retail / bath and sanitary client with 19,000 products and 5,000 spare parts indexed across 20 PDF catalogs. Although deployed in a B2C channel, the retrieval architecture is the same as what you'd need for an internal purchasing or sales search tool.

block2.title: Invoices, delivery notes, and documents into ERP

pain.label: The pain
pain.text: Your admin team spends hours entering invoices and delivery notes into the ERP. Data arrives in different formats depending on the supplier, there are transcription errors, and the bottleneck is always the same: one person copying fields by hand.

solution.label: The solution
solution.text: A pipeline that receives documents by email or folder, extracts the relevant data using AI, cross-references it against your supplier and product master data, and prepares it for ERP upload. Ambiguous cases are flagged for human review before loading.

result.label: The result with a real client
result.text: I built a production invoice verification system for a retail / bath and sanitary client, as part of a loyalty program for professional installers. The system processes 500 invoices/month, extracts the sold products, and matches them against the catalog master with 85–90% accuracy on noisy data (imperfect OCR, abbreviations, partial references). The same architecture works for ERP upload.

pain.label: The pain
pain.text: Your IT or internal support team answers the same questions over and over: "how do I access X?", "where is the Y procedure?", "I need permissions for Z". Repetitive queries consume the team, and the ones that actually need attention wait.

solution.label: The solution
solution.text: A bot integrated in Teams that answers frequent questions from your internal documentation and, when it can't resolve, automatically creates a ticket in your system with the information already collected from the user. The support team receives clean cases, not raw questions.

result.label: The result with a real client
result.text: Support bot deployed in Microsoft Teams for an appraisal and valuation client, with automatic ticket creation from the conversation. Frequently asked questions no longer reach the human team; real cases arrive with context.

pain.label: The pain
pain.text: During an earnings presentation, analysts ask live about figures, charts and acronyms in the deck. Answering on the spot, with the exact figure and without going beyond what was presented, depends on someone finding the right slide in time.

solution.label: The solution
solution.text: An assistant that transcribes questions as they are asked and answers in streaming relying only on the presentation slides, citing which ones each answer comes from. What isn't in the deck, it doesn't make up.

result.label: The result in the datathon
result.text: Built solo in one week for the Turing Datathon, where it took 2nd place. On a synthetic set of 24 questions: 23/24 top-1 accuracy with rephrasings (21/24 without them), 24/24 top-3 and 8/8 in English. The demo processes an audio file; the natural next step is a live microphone.

operations.closingLine: If you recognize any of these pain points in your operation, let's talk. Each case starts from an analysis of the real process, not a template.

case1.title: Multi-agent RAG chat over enterprise applications
case1.meta: Indra Group (via Malt) · Freelance · AI Engineer · May – Oct 2026
case1.summary: Multi-agent chat that answers functional and technical questions about enterprise applications across several clients, configurable to prioritize cost or quality. The challenge: combining code, documentation and a dependency graph while keeping cost per query under control.
decisions: LangGraph orchestration (orchestrator-workers pattern): an analyzer decomposes the question and plans the search, and several workers search and answer in parallel. Configurable with lightweight workers (Claude Haiku) to minimize cost, or with a Claude Sonnet synthesizer over all the evidence to maximize quality

Multi-source retrieval: vector search on S3 Vectors with a per-project index, per-source-type reranking (Cohere Rerank 3.5), logical chunking with a context sentence, and deterministic graph queries with semantic fallback
Rigorous evaluation: CLI harness with repeated runs to measure noise, blind grading and a per-stage loss funnel. Around 180 experiments
Roadmap with measured prototypes, on my own initiative: graph-guided planning (the analyzer receives the project context: nodes and relationships) and more granular workers (−30% cost in prototype)
case1.deliverables: Chat and evaluation harness code, technical documentation and handoff to the team, and a next-steps report with a prioritized recommendation.

case2.title: Voice-based financial Q&A assistant
case2.meta: Turing Datathon · Jul 2026 · 2nd place · solo, in one week
case2.summary: Transcribes analysts' questions during an earnings presentation and answers in streaming, relying only on the slides. The challenge: answering on the spot, sticking to the deck's content and without making things up.
decisions: PPTX ingestion with offline enrichment: textual descriptions of charts, bilingual ES/EN rephrasings and synthetic questions
Hybrid retrieval on pgvector (70% vector, 30% full-text) so figures, years and acronyms aren't lost
Transcription with Azure AI Speech: conservative correction with a dynamic glossary and deterministic question detection, with an LLM only as fallback
Answers that cite only the retrieved slides, streamed question by question
The demo processes an audio file; the natural next step is a live microphone

production1.title: Conversational assistant over product catalog
production1.meta: Sector: Retail / Bath & Sanitary · Wembley Studios · 2024
production1.summary: Conversational system over ~20 supplier PDF catalogs, ~19,000 products, and ~5,000 spare parts. The main challenge was not generation — it was retrieval: catalogs had inconsistent structures, reference mismatches, and technical data in poorly scanned tables.
decisions: Hybrid search (lexical + vector) to combine exact reference matches with semantic search
Semantic ranking on results to prioritize actual relevance
Multi-query retrieval to decompose complex questions
Tool-calling routing to avoid invoking the LLM when a deterministic query sufficed

production2.title: Automatic invoice verification in a loyalty program
production2.meta: Sector: Retail / Bath & Sanitary · Wembley Studios · 2024
production2.summary: B2B loyalty system where professional installers upload invoices from their distributors and earn points for the brand's products sold. The technical challenge was not generic extraction — it was reliable identification: in a multi-brand distributor invoice, you need to identify which products belong to the client brand, which references map to which catalog SKU, all with noisy input data (imperfect OCR, abbreviations, partial references).
decisions: Azure Document Intelligence for structured extraction of invoice line items
Embeddings + fuzzy matching + layered heuristics for product matching against the catalog master with noisy data
Measured accuracy of 85–90% in matching against master data
Asynchronous architecture with Azure Functions and Service Bus for volume spike tolerance (500 invoices/month)
Human validation before crediting points on all processed cases

production3.title: Internal support bot on Teams
production3.summary: Conversational bot integrated in Microsoft Teams that answers questions about internal documentation and, when it cannot resolve, opens a ticket in the management system with the context already collected from the user.
decisions: RAG over internal document base with per-user access control
Intent detection to distinguish resolvable queries vs. incidents requiring a ticket
Enriched ticket creation: the bot extracts data from the conversation (affected system, problem description, urgency) and structures it before creating the incident

about.title: Manuel Romero
bio: I'm Manuel Romero. I've been building generative AI systems for B2B since 2023.

I started as AI Engineer at Wembley Studios, a B2B technical consultancy, where over two years I designed and deployed production systems for real clients: a conversational assistant over product catalogs with 19,000 references in retail, a loyalty system with automatic invoice verification for professionals in the same sector, and an internal support bot integrated with Teams for a company in the appraisal and valuation sector. These were not POCs or demos — they are systems still running today.

Since March 2025 I work as a freelancer, and I'm a Super Malter on Malt. My current focus is three specific services where I can deliver deep value: agents and RAG systems, document automation with AI, and GenAI architecture. I prefer going slow and specializing rather than offering a broad catalog without depth.

In 2026, via Malt, I built a multi-agent RAG chat over enterprise applications on AWS Bedrock for Indra Group, and took 2nd place in the Turing Datathon with a voice-based financial Q&A assistant. Since April 2026 I also work with LILT, designing Spanish-language programming tasks to train and evaluate AI agents for leading AI labs.

I have production systems on Azure (with three official certifications: AI-102, DP-100, AZ-204) and have built multi-agent systems on AWS Bedrock, using the Python AI ecosystem: LangChain, LangGraph, FastAPI, PostgreSQL with pgvector. But technology is the tool; what I sell is the judgment to decide what to build, how, and what not to build, with quality and cost measured through systematic evaluation. The specialization is in the problem, not in the vendor's logo.

howIWork.title: Connect. Disconnect. Reconnect.
howIWork.intro: Building an AI system in a company is not just deploying code. It means understanding the real process, integrating it into operations, and making the team adopt it. My way of working comes down to three words.

step1.title: Connect
step1.subtitle: Before proposing architecture, I understand the process.
step1.body:
Every company has its own way of working, its tools, its real bottlenecks (which are almost never the ones that appear in the initial brief). The first job is to identify where AI adds real value and where it's more efficient not to use it. Not every process needs an LLM behind it; some just need a well-written SQL query or a procedure change.

This phase is conversation, observation, and a lot of questions. The goal is to come out with a clear map of what to build, what not to build, and why.

step2.title: Disconnect
step2.subtitle: The system runs so your team doesn't have to babysit it.
step2.body:
Once the use case is identified, I build it so that repetitive work stops going through people. Invoices are processed automatically, frequent queries are resolved without intervention, data is centralized and queryable. What used to take hours now happens in the background.

The goal is not just to automate tasks — it's to free up attention. To let your team stop spending energy on the mechanical so they can spend it on what requires judgment.

step3.title: Reconnect
step3.subtitle: Less operational noise, more room for what matters.
step3.body:
When the system works, something happens that goes beyond ROI: people stop rushing around all day. The operations manager leaves at 6pm instead of 9pm. The CTO stops fighting fires and starts thinking three months ahead. The team stops being scattered and starts having mental space.

It sounds soft for a technical service, but it's the result I see again and again. A well-built system doesn't just save costs; it returns time and lowers the temperature of operations. And that time is what you decide how to use: on strategy, on the team, or on your life outside of work.
